Let <MATH_0001>,
<MATH_0002> be functors over <MATH_0003>, and let
<MATH_0004>,
<MATH_0005> be isomorphisms of
functors over <MATH_0006>. By
Categories, Lemma <REF_0001>
we see that <MATH_0007> is fibred if and only if <MATH_0008>
is fibred over <MATH_0009>. Hence we may assume that both
<MATH_0010> and <MATH_0011> are fibred. Moreover, the proof of
Categories, Lemma <REF_0002>
shows that <MATH_0012> and <MATH_0013> map strongly cartesian morphisms to strongly
cartesian morphisms, i.e., <MATH_0014> and <MATH_0015> are <MATH_0016>-morphisms of fibred
categories over <MATH_0017>. This means that given
<MATH_0018>, and <MATH_0019> then
the presheaves
<MATH_0020>
are identified, see
Lemma <REF_0003>. Hence
the first is a sheaf if and only if the second is a sheaf.
Finally, we have to show that if every descent datum in <MATH_0021>
is effective, then so is every descent datum in <MATH_0022>.
To do this, let <MATH_0023> be a descent datum
in <MATH_0024> relative the covering <MATH_0025> of the site
<MATH_0026>. Then <MATH_0027> is a descent datum
in <MATH_0028> relative the covering <MATH_0029>.
Let <MATH_0030> be an object of <MATH_0031> such that the
descent datum <MATH_0032> is isomorphic to
<MATH_0033>. Then <MATH_0034> is an object of <MATH_0035>
such that the descent datum <MATH_0036> is isomorphic to
<MATH_0037> which in turn is isomorphic to
the original descent datum <MATH_0038> using <MATH_0039>.
